title: Tangent sections and effective zero divisors of smooth-curve derivations
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be a smooth proper connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], and let $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be its genus [def-sc-genus]. Write $\Omega^1_{X/k}$ for the sheaf of relative differentials with universal derivation $d$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], and $T=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\Omega^1_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$ for its dual. Then $T$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], of degree $2-2g$ [def-sc-pic0], and the universal derivation gives a canonical additive identification
$$\operatorname{Der}_k(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_X)\cong H^0(X,T),\qquad D=\theta\circ d\longleftrightarrow\theta.$$
Here derivations are $k$-linear sheaf maps satisfying the Leibniz rule, and $H^0(X,T)$ means global sections. Every closed point $q$ has residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. A derivation $D$ preserves the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_q$ [def-sfb-curve-vector-fields-fixing-points] if and only if its corresponding section $s_D$ of $T$ vanishes in the fibre at $q$. For every nonzero $D$, $s_D$ has nonzero generic germ, and its rational-section divisor
$$Z_D=\operatorname{div}_T(s_D)=\sum_{q\ \mathrm{closed}}m_q[q]$$
[def-sc-rational-section-divisor, def-sc-divisor] is effective, has finite support, and satisfies $T\cong\mathcal O_X(Z_D)$ and $\deg Z_D=\sum_qm_q=2-2g$. Its coefficient $m_q$ is the valuation of the local coefficient of $s_D$ in any basis of $T_q$; it is positive exactly when $D(\mathcal I_q)\subseteq\mathcal I_q$. In particular each distinct point fixed by a nonzero $D$ contributes at least one to this degree.

proof.text: Apply the smooth connected curve local-ring theorem: $X$ is Noetherian and integral, its generic stalk is its function field, and each closed stalk is a DVR. Apply the closed-point residue-field theorem to the finite-type $k$-scheme $X$: the structural map $k\to\kappa(q)$ is an isomorphism for every closed $q$. In particular this residue extension is finite separable, as required for the uniformizer differential lemma.

source.place: Tag 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields), standing hypotheses; Tag 0C1E (lemma-uniformizer-works), residue hypothesis; morphisms.tex Tag 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points)

proof.text: The diagonal-conormal comparison identifies the canonical differential sheaf used by the curve lemmas with the affine universal differential sheaf in this statement. By the canonical-sheaf lemma $\Omega^1_{X/k}$ is invertible; the tensor-dual lemma makes $T=(\Omega^1_{X/k})^\vee$ invertible and gives $\Omega^1_{X/k}\otimes T\cong\mathcal O_X$. By the canonical-degree lemma choose $K$ with $\mathcal O_X(K)\cong\Omega^1_{X/k}$ and $\deg K=2g-2$. Since the degree on the Picard group is a homomorphism, $\deg\Omega^1_{X/k}=2g-2$ and $\deg T=-(2g-2)=2-2g$.

source.place: Tag 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields), proof, tangent degree; Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), 0BS6 (lemma-rr); divisors.tex Tag 02SL (lemma-c1-additive); morphisms.tex Tag 08S2 (lemma-differentials-diagonal).

proof.text: By the universal property of the sheaf of relative differentials, applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, composition with $d$ is an additive bijection from $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\theta:\Omega^1_{X/k}\to\mathcal O_X$ onto $k$-derivations $D:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$; here a $k$-derivation is a $k$-linear Leibniz sheaf map, i.e. one killing the constants, which is the stated notion. The sheaf-Hom definition identifies these global morphisms $\theta$ with $H^0(X,T)$. Write $s_D$ for the section corresponding to $\theta$ with $D=\theta\circ d$. Additivity is $(\theta+\theta')\circ d=\theta\circ d+\theta'\circ d$. This gives exactly the stated canonical additive identification.

source.place: Tag 01UR (lemma-universal-derivation-universal); curves.tex Tag 0E67, first sentence of the proof

proof.text: Fix a closed point $q$ and choose a uniformizer $t$ of $A=\mathcal O_{X,q}$. Smoothness implies local finite presentation. Apply the current affine-chart stalk theorem over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: choose $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $q$, with $q$ represented by $\mathfrak p$, so $A\cong B_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\Omega^1_{X/k,q}\cong(\Omega_{B/k})_{\mathfrak p}$. The localization theorem identifies the latter with $\Omega_{A/k}$, sending $db/1$ to $d(b/1)$. These comparisons preserve the universal derivation: on fractions, Leibniz gives $d(b/u)=u^{-1}db-bu^{-2}du$ for $u\notin\mathfrak p$. The uniformizer differential lemma applies by step 1 and gives the basis $dt$ of $\Omega^1_{X/k,q}$. In the dual basis write $(s_D)_q=a(dt)^\vee$, so $a=\theta_q(dt)=D_q(t)$. Since $\mathfrak m_q=(t)$, the Leibniz formula $D_q(bt)=bD_q(t)+tD_q(b)$ shows $D_q(\mathfrak m_q)\subseteq\mathfrak m_q$ if and only if $a\in\mathfrak m_q$. Away from $q$ the point ideal stalk is the whole local ring, so there is no condition. Membership in a subsheaf is local, hence preservation of the ideal sheaf is equivalent to this stalk condition. Finally the image of $s_D$ in $T_q/\mathfrak m_qT_q$ is zero exactly when $a\in\mathfrak m_q$. This proves the fixed-point/fibre-vanishing equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0C1E (lemma-uniformizer-works); Tag 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields), final paragraph and fixed-point definition preceding the lemma; algebra.tex Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), (2); morphisms.tex Tag 01UT.

proof.text: Let $D\ne0$. By step 3 its global section $s_D$ is nonzero. A section of an invertible module on $X$ with zero generic germ is zero: on a nonempty trivializing open it is a regular function with zero generic germ, and the injectivity in the local-ring theorem makes that function zero. These opens cover $X$. Thus $s_D$ has nonzero generic germ. At every closed $q$, express its stalk as $a_q e_q$ in a basis. The generic germ of $e_q$ is a basis, by local trivialization, so $a_q\ne0$. Since $a_q\in\mathcal O_{X,q}$, its normalized valuation is nonnegative; it is positive exactly when $a_q\in\mathfrak m_q$ (write $a_q=ut^n$ in the DVR). A different basis multiplies $a_q$ by a unit and leaves its valuation unchanged.

source.place: Tag 02SF (definition-order-vanishing-meromorphic), preceding paragraph; curves.tex Tag 0E67, nonzero tangent section

proof.text: Apply the rational-section order theorem to the nonzero generic germ of $s_D$ in the invertible module $T$: only finitely many of its orders $m_q$ are nonzero, and the rational-section divisor definition gives $Z_D=\sum_qm_q[q]$. Step 5 makes this an effective divisor. The line-bundle rational-section theorem gives the isomorphism $\mathcal O_X(Z_D)\to T$, $f\mapsto fs_D$. The defining degree homomorphism therefore gives $\deg Z_D=\deg T=2-2g$; the divisor degree is $\sum_qm_q$, since the points have residue field $k$. By step 4 and the local computation in step 5, $m_q>0$ holds exactly when $D$ preserves $\mathcal I_q$. Every such integer is at least one, so every distinct fixed point contributes at least one to the sum, as claimed.
